sections.brief: Open the stage with the change of president: the 1944 Wallace–Truman vice-presidential swap, FDR's death on 12 April 1945 (one week after his 5 April letter to Ibn Saud — link to [scene:s07ca|FDR and Ibn Saud] rather than retelling Bitter Lake), and Truman arriving with no foreign-policy experience. Then set out the cast that recurs through the stage — Clifford and his November 1947 memo, Marshall's threat to resign, Jacobson's 18 March 1948 meeting, the State Department (Henderson, Lovett) — using every deep-dive section on trum and clif, but tell the memo, the March meeting and the recognition only as far as needed and link forward to s07j, rd5_trusteeship and rec_s01. Present the motive dispute fairly: the scene's 'domestic calculation' reading against Truman's own stated humanitarian conviction (developed in tr_s01 and wh_s01); the scene's counterfactual about Wallace is a reading, not a finding, and must be labeled so. Figure: a power-structure tree of who advised Truman on Palestine and who opposed (from the scene's entities).

Truman's own documented words before any 1948 campaign money, in order: the April 1943 Chicago Stadium rally (as a senator), the 10 November 1945 meeting with the chiefs of mission (the official record vs. William Eddy's single-witness 1954 account of the 'hundreds of thousands' remark — say plainly that Eddy opposed Zionism), the 1947 diary entry released in 2003 after Morgenthau's call about the Exodus refugees, and the eleven-minute recognition. The section's point is that conviction, irritation and electoral arithmetic coexist in the record; do not resolve which drove him. Figure: a timeline of the five dated items.

The July 1945 meeting in Rudolf Sonneborn's Manhattan apartment and the network it founded, using every deep-dive section of sonneborn45, mfp and shield, plus fis_s01 (17 businessmen, Feinberg, the dd-flow mechanism and enforcement table) and the 1940s portions of cia_s01 (the Shai's budget and staff in 1948, Rekhesh, the FBI-recommends/DOJ-declines FARA pattern) and fis_s04 (the OSS Palestine desk, kept brief). Flag the source conflict: s07d names the front 'Materials for Palestine', fis_s01 'Materials for Israel'; fis_s01 dates the meeting 1 July 1945. Keep the shield entity's Abba Hillel Silver liaison claim at the scene's own strength. Link Feinberg's later story forward to [scene:s07f2|Abraham Feinberg]. Figures: embed global_funding:Defense Money:0 and a money chain (donors → Sonneborn Institute → front company → purchases/transit → Haganah).

Ernest Bevin, the gap the series has never filled: Labour's victory (26 July 1945), Bevin at the Foreign Office, his 13 November 1945 statement (the joint committee, immigration at the 'present monthly rate', trusteeship) and Winant's report that he would 'stake his political future' on a solution; the 'head of the queue' and 'too many Jews in New York' remarks (June 1946); the London (Lancaster House) conference of September 1946 and his US visit. Present the dispute over his motives with all three positions and their named historians (Mayhew/Weizmann/Weiler; Bullock/Ben-Gurion/Attlee; Beeley's oil-and-Suez briefing and Louis), ending with Langham's conclusion — name the antisemitic remarks plainly as what they were without converting them into a finding about policy. Figure: a timeline of Bevin's Palestine decisions 1945–46; link forward to rd5_britain_exits.

The Anglo-American Committee of Inquiry, announced November 1945 (link back to rd5_bevin for Bevin's announcement): its twelve members, hearings on three continents January–March 1946 (Hourani for the Arab Office, Magnes and Ihud for a binational state), the unanimous April 1946 report (100,000 certificates, repeal of the 1940 land regulations, 'neither a Jewish nor an Arab state'), Truman's endorsement of the 100,000 alone, Britain's disarmament condition, and Morrison–Grady (July 1946) rejected by both sides. Use every deep-dive section. Figure: a comparison of what the report recommended and what Washington and London each took from it.

The Jewish Resistance Movement: the September 1945 agreement among Haganah (via the Palmah), Irgun and Lehi; the Night of the Trains (1 November 1945) and the Night of the Bridges (17 June 1946); the halt decided in August and confirmed in Basel on 9 December 1946. State plainly that the only source is the Lehi heritage association and attribute accordingly; no casualty totals are established. Link back to [scene:s07e2|Irgun and Lehi] for the organizations' origins and forward to s07e3. Figure: a timeline from September 1945 to December 1946.

Operation Agatha, 29 June 1946: 17,000 troops and police, more than 2,700 arrests including Jewish Agency leaders, and the documents seized from the Agency, with the name 'Black Sabbath' explained; use every deep-dive section of kdh_becomes_target (physical layout, motive). Place it as Britain's answer to the united resistance (rd5_revolt, which ended the Night of the Bridges twelve days earlier) and end on the documented line to the bombing three weeks later. Figure: process flow from the Night of the Bridges to Agatha to the King David plan.

The King David Hotel bombing, 22 July 1946: 91 dead (British, Arab and Jewish), Begin's command, the disputed warning calls (give both the Irgun account of calls ~25 minutes before and the British/historians' dispute over receipt), the Jewish Agency's condemnation despite its own role in the resistance movement, and the hardening of British opinion. Answer the reader's question whether this ended the united resistance (rd5_revolt records the August 1946 halt). Figure: key figures (date, dead, time of warning as claimed).

The Jewish Agency's diplomatic preparation: the August 1946 partition proposal and partition as avowed policy by 1946, a year before UNSCOP. Relate it to the Agency's executive meeting in Paris that same August (rd5_revolt notes the halt to armed action decided there) without adding facts not in the material. Keep the 'resemblance to the West Bank' at the source's strength. Link forward to s07i.

Inside the White House 1945–48: David Niles (one of two FDR aides Truman kept), Max Lowenthal, Jacobson's separate channel (link to s08), and the 4 October 1946 Yom Kippur statement a month before the midterms, with Attlee's anger. Present Reston's politics reading and Truman's February 1947 rebuttal side by side, and the synthesis that both can be true. Embed the info_war map and discuss its 'White House channel' node.

How Britain left: the Cabinet decision of 14 February 1947 and Bevin's 18 February 'irreconcilable conflict of principles' statement (attribute the COJS text; give the 1,200,000/600,000 figures he used); the UK's 2 April 1947 request (A/286); the executions of April 1947, the Acre break-in, the sergeants affair (dates only) and the anti-Jewish riots in Britain; the Exodus 1947 (give the 17 vs 18 July discrepancy) and Bevin's insistence on return to France and then Hamburg — link to [scene:ab_s01|Aliyah Bet] for the clandestine fleet; Creech Jones's 26 September statement; Britain's abstention. Present the dispute over how much the insurgency caused the withdrawal. Embed global_funding:Budgets & Britain:1 and discuss Britain's 1945–47 military bill. Figure: a timeline February–September 1947.

The Soviet layer: Gromyko's 14 May 1947 speech (one state preferred, partition acceptable), the bloc's votes in November 1947, its stand when Washington wavered in March 1948 (link to rd5_trusteeship), the first de jure recognition on 17 May 1948, and the vote against Resolution 194 in December 1948 (link forward to [scene:rr_s01|Resolution 194]). Present the 'remove Britain' motive as the analysts' reading it is. Link the arms to cz_s01.

UNSCOP from the record: the special session (28 April), Resolution 106 (S-1) of 15 May 1947 and Australia's 13–11–29 membership vote, the eleven members, Sandström, the arrival on 14–15 June, the Arab Higher Committee's boycott letters of 13 June and 10 July, the hearing of six Arab governments in Beirut on 22 July and the Amman visit, the Jewish Agency witnesses (Ben-Gurion's testimony and map from the scene; Shertok, Horowitz, Weizmann from the report), the DP-camp visit (8–14 August), and the 7–3 majority/minority split with Australia abstaining. Correct the scene's own claim that the committee heard 'almost exclusively' one side: Palestinian bodies boycotted, but Arab governments were heard — present both. Note the CIE '8 of 11' figure as an error against the report. Figure: comparison of the majority and minority plans and who backed each.

The written warnings of September–October 1947: Henderson's 22 September memo to Marshall, the Joint Chiefs' 10 October memorandum, Forrestal's 'life blood of a war machine' testimony and ARAMCO's lobbying, then Truman's decision; use every deep-dive section on all five entities. Name who warned and who prevailed (Clifford) without suggesting a single hidden hand — this is convergence and conflict inside one government. Embed the warnings_1947 map and walk through its nodes.

US intelligence from the OSS (Donovan) through the Central Intelligence Group to the CIA (18 September 1947, Hillenkoetter), and ORE-55 of 28 November 1947, the day before the vote: its predictions of armed hostilities, early Jewish advantage and damage to US interests. Draw cia_s02 only for its 1947–48 warnings and the 6:11 pm recognition (link Angleton and the later partnership forward to [scene:cia_s02|1948: CIA Opposes]); flag that cia_s02's claim that a CIA report predicted an embargo would bring 'peaceful coexistence' is not in ORE-55's summary. Figure: timeline of the four warnings (State, JCS, Defense, CIA) against the vote.

Who objected at the time: the American Council for Judaism (Rosenwald, Berger) and its 1948 objection to UJA money for 'political and foreign governmental purposes', the American Jewish Committee's 1944 trusteeship proposal, Kermit Roosevelt Jr.'s 1948 pamphlet, the Gildersleeve committee — and, from the research, Arendt's May 1948 'To Save the Jewish Homeland', Magnes's May 1948 meeting with Truman, and the 4 December 1948 Einstein–Arendt letter on Begin's Herut. Give the ACJ's own and Zionist sources' assessments of its size. Note that the letter's Deir Yassin toll (240) is the 1948 figure; link to ma_s01 for current scholarship. Link enforcement in 1962–63 forward.

Resolution 181, using every deep-dive section of flip and forr: the Ad Hoc Committee vote of 25 November (25–13–17), the shortfall and three-day postponement, the three states that moved (Haiti, Liberia, the Philippines; Firestone per Michael Cohen), Forrestal's 'bullying' diary entries, the final 33–13–10 with the full lists of those against and abstaining, the Arab delegations' statements, the timetable (1 August / 1 February / 1 April / 1 October 1948) and the five-state Palestine Commission. Present the population and land dispute in full (Yusuf 498,000/494,000 vs Sachar 538,000/397,000; 56% vs the scene's 55%; ~7% Jewish ownership from iaa_s03 and Yusuf's 6%/10%) and the Jewish Agency's and Arab arguments in their strongest forms. Embed money_1948:Land & People:1 and prestate_funding:Overview:0 and the state_build map; figure: a comparison of the Jewish and Arab states by area and population with both sources.

Palestinian Arab agency and its limits, 1945–48: the Arab League's line from March 1945, its reconstitution of the Arab Higher Committee in 1946, the Mufti's escape from France to Cairo (May 1946) and chairmanship, the League's sessions (boycott, land fund, Bludan, rejection of partition, Aley's military preparations, the December 1947 decision against formal intervention, February 1948 measures), the Mufti's failed pleas for a shadow government and the League's refusal (February 1948), then — telling forward in brief — the All-Palestine Government (20 and 22 September, 30 September 1948 council) and the Jericho Congress (1 December 1948). Name the Mufti's wartime Axis alliance plainly in one sentence and link to [scene:s07a5|the Arab Revolt and Berlin]. Present the dispute over who spoke for the Palestinians. Figure: power structure of Arab decision-making on Palestine in 1947–48 (League Council and Political Committee, AHC, Arab Liberation Army, Army of the Holy War, Transjordan).

Two escalations, not one: the clean vote split (Jewish Agency acceptance with reservations; Arab League and Arab Higher Committee rejection, Jamal Husseini's 'line of fire and blood'), then the civil war from 1 December 1947 with attacks in both directions as the scene documents them, the Arab Liberation Army (Qawuqji) and the Army of the Holy War (Abd al-Qadir al-Husayni, killed at al-Qastal 8 April 1948), Gush Etzion, and the separate state invasion of 15 May (link to rd5_invasion). State the strongest form of both readings — 'the Arabs rejected and attacked' and 'a two-sided war began at once' — and show which parts of each the record supports. Figure: timeline November 1947 – 15 May 1948.

What the vote set off for Jews in the Arab world: the riots of 30 November–5 December 1947 (Aleppo and the Codex, Aden, Bahrain, Damascus, Cairo, Beirut), Egypt's arrests, sequestrations and the Cairo bombings of June–September 1948 (with the Brotherhood trial), Iraq's July 1948 law and Shafiq Ades (from irq_e04, including Iraq's refusal to sign an armistice), Aleppo's arrests, Tripoli, and Yemen's December 1948 exit permission. Present the Aden and Cairo toll disputes; identify the 1951 Anderson study for what it is. Use me_s07 only for the 1948–70s total (800,000–900,000) and oa_s03 only for Morocco's post-1948 emigration; link to [scene:s00e3|two displacements] and forward to the airlifts. Name the antisemitic violence plainly; do not generalize about Arabs or Muslims — tie each act to a named government, mob, or organization.

Golda Meyerson's US tour, January–March 1948: Kaplan's failure to raise $7 million, Montor (the same man who gathered the 1945 Sonneborn group), the Chicago Council of Jewish Federations speech, about $25 million in the first month and the $5 million Chicago loan, and a reported $50 million on her 19 March return, spent largely on weapons including Czech arms; Ben-Gurion's 'money which made the state possible'. Keep 'reported' where the scene does. Embed money_1948:Dollar Flows:0, global_funding:Where It Went:0 and global_funding:Year by Year:1 and discuss the 1948 UJA total and the Palestine share; figure: money chain from donors to arms.

The arms network in operation 1945–48: the transit countries (Czechoslovakia, Panama, Mexico, Canada, France), Schwimmer's air operation, the January 1948 New Jersey crate (one of 76), the 1950 Los Angeles trial and the pardons; add fis_s02 (800 shipments, ~2,400 tons, the Neutrality Act embargo it dates 14 December 1947, Winters) and fis_s03 (the FBI's separate wiretaps on the ZOA and Sol Rotenberg for suspected Communist ties — keep the two FBI concerns distinct). Flag the conflicts between scenes: Lineas Aereas de Panama vs Service Airways; Winters's two vs three B-17s and $5,000 fine; Schwimmer's pardon in 2000 vs 2001; Winters's pardon by Bush in 2008 vs 'Clinton in 2001'. Figure: process flow from purchase to transit to Palestine.

The Czechoslovak pipeline: the 14 January 1948 contract via Secretariat D, before the state and before Resolution 46 (17 April 1948); Operation Balak from Žatec ('Zebra') to Ekron, May–August 1948; about 25 Avia S-199s forming 101 Squadron; some 35,000 Kar 98k rifles; Široký's 1952 figure of almost $14.5 million; Soviet consent; Ben-Gurion's 1968 verdict. Present the price dispute ($14.5 million to ~$90 million in the funding ledger). Embed global_funding:The Arms Bill:0, money_1948:Overview:0 and aid_arms:Overview:2 (US economic aid only, 1948–61) and discuss each. Link the Soviet diplomacy to so_s01.

Plan Dalet, 10 March 1948: the text first (objective clause, the village clause 4(b) quoted exactly), the earlier Plans B (September 1945) and C (May 1946), and Khalidi's list of operations from Nachshon (1 April) to 14 May with their stated objectives — say these are Khalidi's translations. Then the three readings side by side without adjudication: Khalidi 1961/1988 and Pappé (master plan), Morris (military plan with local discretion), and the scene's synthesis. Note Khalidi's own correction that at least ten villages were captured before 1 March. Figure: timeline of the operations listed.

Washington's retreat, March 1948: Austin's 19 March statement that partition 'cannot now be implemented by peaceful means' and the proposed temporary trusteeship, suspension of the Palestine Commission, Lie's reaction, Arab delegates' reaction, Silver's 'shocking reversal' and Ben-Gurion's 20 March refusal. Place it the day after Jacobson brought Weizmann to Truman (s08) and explain why the two events collided; link the Soviet stand to so_s01. Figure: comparison of the US position in November 1947 and March 1948.

Deir Yassin (9 April 1948; long cited as 254, current scholarship about 110, the Red Cross report of ~150 bodies, classified archives), the Hadassah convoy (13 April, 78 Jews killed) and Tantura (the retracted thesis, the 2022 veterans' testimony, the denials, the unknown toll). Give equal care to atrocities against Jews and against Arabs, and show how the record grew from Israeli archives, students and veterans. Note that December 1948's Einstein–Arendt letter gave 240 (see rf_s01). Figure: key figures with each count's source.

The fall of the mixed towns in April–May 1948: Khalidi's point that territory was held only from 1 April; Tiberias (18 April); Haifa (21–22 April) in detail — the Carmeli Brigade, Stockwell's redeployment, British casualty figures, the Town Hall meeting, and the exodus; then a phrase each for Jaffa, Safed, Beisan and Acre linked to pd_s01's operation list. Present the Haifa dispute with all three positions (Khalidi's expulsion-and-collusion account, the Jewish Chronicle's account of Shabtai Levy's plea — flagged as opinion without archival citation — and Morris's shifting position as Khalidi reports it), and the 50,000 vs ~60,000 departure figures. Figure: timeline of the towns' fall.

Abdullah between the Jewish Agency, Britain and the Arab League: the Naharayim meeting (November 1947), the February 1948 Bevin–Abu al-Huda–Glubb meeting and Jevon's corroboration of the 'green light', the Arab League's 30 April decision and Abdullah as commander-in-chief, Meyerson's 10 May journey to Amman, Shimoni's verdict, Quwwatli's 15 May halt request. Then the Arab Legion's war (from ijr_src_s05: East Jerusalem and the West Bank) with the 1950 annexation and its three recognitions told in a sentence and linked forward. Present the collusion debate in its strongest forms on both sides. Figure: a timeline November 1947 – 15 May 1948.

Independence on 14 May 1948 and the Nakba, using every deep-dive section of cz, nak (the numbers, Plan Dalet, Deir Yassin, Childers's 1961 radio-broadcast finding, the Czech arms, effects on Palestine and the region) and child. Add the Declaration's own text: its grounds, the equality clause, the appeal to Arab inhabitants and neighbours, no stated borders, the 1 October 1948 constitution deadline — and link that promise to ilgov_s01 (tell only that the constitution never came; link forward). Treat the coexist entity's millennium claim and flagChoice as labeled readings. The 'Arab radio' myth gets both Childers's evidence and Morris's ≤5% figure (rd5_refugees). Keep detailed refugee numbers for rd5_refugees and arms for cz_s01, linking. Embed year_ledger:Part 5:0.

Who recognizes a nation: Article II, Section 3; Zivotofsky v. Kerry (2015); the press release eleven minutes after the proclamation (de facto) and de jure recognition on 31 January 1949; Congress's indirect role. Set beside it the Soviet de jure recognition of 17 May (so_s01), Britain's grudging recognition in January 1949 (rd5_britain_exits), the reported 1947 approach to Jinnah (ipk_s07 — say it rests on secondary reporting) and the Vatican's refusal (vat_s01's 1948–49 portion only, including the 1949 UN campaign; link 1993 forward). Note the 6:11 pm time given in cia_s02 (see ore_s01). Figure: comparison of who recognized when, and on what basis.

The Arab states' war: the Arab League's 15 May cablegram (S/745) in its own words, including its claim of over a quarter of a million displaced; the armies (Egypt, Transjordan, Syria, Lebanon — with ilb_s02 on Lebanon's own decision and smallest army — Iraq, and Saudi Arabia's contingent under Egyptian command per isa_src_s02, with the 1948 boycott); the first round (Latrun, the Jewish Quarter, Degania, Ashdod), the first truce (11 June–9 July, Bernadotte, his plan), the Ten Days and Lydda–Ramla (Operation Dani, 'Expel them', Rabin's order, the competing tolls), the second truce (18 July), and the armistices of 1949 (Egypt and Gaza from egi_src_s02; Syria from sy_s01, with Za'im's 1949 offer told in a sentence and linked). Give the force-balance dispute (Shlaim's 35,000 vs 20,000–25,000) and leave the full military-balance argument to s10b. Israeli dead: more than 6,000, about 1% of the Jewish population. Figure: timeline 14 May 1948 – 1949.

The actual military balance: the July 1948 US assessment (~90,000 Israeli forces, ~35,000 in active operations; Arab advantage in artillery and tanks then) — flag that the scene calls it both a CIA and a State Department report — the two phases, Glubb's disputed figures, and the roughly 2:1 Israeli advantage by the end. Set Shlaim's 15 May figures (rd5_invasion) against it without merging the dates. Show why neither popular story survives. Figure: key figures by phase, each dated.

From three militias to one army: the 26 May 1948 order, the Altalena (22 June; Rabin's units; sixteen Irgun members and three soldiers killed), the killing of Bernadotte by Lehi (17 September 1948), the arrests and the February 1949 amnesty, and the later premierships of Begin and Shamir. Link to rf_s01 for the December 1948 Einstein–Arendt letter on Begin's new party. Figure: process flow from order to absorption.

The refugees: how many (the UN technical estimate of about 711,000 from 1949 and its method; PRRN's 726,000, 957,000, 520,000 and 850,000 with their sources; the Arab League's 'quarter of a million' by 15 May in rd5_invasion), where they went (thirds to the West Bank, Gaza and the neighbouring states; hma_src_s02's 1948 node), why they left (the June 1948 IDF intelligence estimate, Morris's conclusions, Khalidi's and Shlaim's dissent), the cabinet's June 1948 consensus against return and Weitz's report, and the village counts (369, 418, 531 and the others, by method). Tell sq_s20 only for what began in 1948 and link Jordan's 1954 law, Lebanon and the present forward; link Resolution 194 and Lausanne to [scene:rr_s01|Resolution 194] and [scene:lau_s01|Lausanne]. Embed money_1948:Land & People:2. Figure: comparison of the refugee estimates by source and method.
